newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end sharply down on labour unrest.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end sharply down on labour unrest.

text.p: Seoul stocks fell sharply across the board on Monday after sentiment was undermined by spreading labour unrest, brokers said.
"This is having a very big impact on the market," said broker Jay Kwon of Hanhwa Securities.
The composite stock index fell 16.54 points to provisionally close at 626.87. Declining shares eclipsed advancers, 763 to 70, while only 17.6 million shares changed hands.
"The market is depressed. Everyone feels that at this rate the index could fall through the 600 support level," said Rhee Joo-ik of Daewoo Securities.

Labour strikes flared again with renewed militancy on Monday after prosecutors summoned top union leaders for questioning. Almost 150,000 workers walked out, calling for a repeal of a controversial new labour bill.

Production at auto makers and other major industries came to a standstill. Hyundai Motor shares were flat at 20,000 won, while Ssangyong Motor fell 200 won to 10,000. Daewoo Heavy lost 10 won to 5,100.
Brokers said President Kim Young-sam's New Year news conference, scheduled for 10.00 a.m. (0100 GMT) on Tuesday, was not expected to boost the market.
"No one is holding out much hope for good news that will rescue the market," Rhee said. "Investors are pulling their money out and moving it to safer ground."
Individual construction shares rose on hopes that strong crude oil prices could spark a construction boom in oil-exporting countries, brokers said.
Dong Ah Construction gained 200 won to 20,200, and Il Sung Construction rose 100 won to 7,500.
